title: Synthesis --- What You Understand, and What You Don't

lessons.title: Synthesis — what you understand, and what you don't
lessons.gloss: synthesis — the sentence you have been saying since chapter 14, finally taken apart

segments.text: Say the sentence you learned in the repair kit, the one that rescues a conversation. (No entiendo.)

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: the formula was a verb all along

segments.text: You have been saying no entiendo since the repair kit, and until four chapters ago it was a single frozen block — two sounds that meant I'm lost, with no moving parts.
It has parts now. Entiendo is entender, and entender is Latin intendere, "to stretch toward." Which means the sentence you have been using to admit defeat has never actually said I failed. It says:
I am not managing to stretch that far.
That was true the whole time. You just could not see it yet.
And the moment a formula has parts, it turns. No entiendo stops being the only thing you can say and becomes one option among several.
Back in the repair kit, all you could do:
— No entiendo. Más despacio, por favor.
Now, the same moment, with the parts working:
— Perdón — leo un poco, pero no entiendo. — Más despacio, por favor. Ahora entiendo. Gracias.
Same trouble. But the second speaker is no longer only failing — they are reporting which part works and which does not. That is the difference between a distress signal and a conversation.
Four verbs is not four words. It is the ability to say where you are in a language: what you take in, what you work on, what lands, what you can produce.

segments.text: Run the second one until it sounds like a person, not a repair kit.

segments.prompt: What does no entiendo literally say, given intendere?
acceptedResponses: i am not stretching that far
i am not reaching that far

feedback.correct: Yes — not a confession of failure, a report of reach.
feedback.incorrect: Intendere is to stretch toward: I am not managing to stretch that far.

segments.prompt: How do you say I understand now, once it slows down?

segments.text: Which verb was hiding inside no entiendo? (Entender.) What did it physically mean? (To stretch toward.) What can you say now that you could not say back then? (Not just that you are lost — which part is lost.)
